answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil clusters via bounded random walks over a staked trust graph seeded by a randomness beacon. Honest peers form a dense reef of mutual attestations, so fake clusters meet the core across a narrow bridge of attack edges that limits walk intersections. Requiring slashable stake per vouch forces attackers to lock capital and secure scarce trusted links per identity. However, wealthy adversaries can still buy endorsements from colluding insiders.
